item.title: Christian Siriano invites New York Fashion Week guests into his surrealist dream

item.title: Trump pardons 5 former NFL players for crimes ranging from perjury to drug trafficking
item.description: President Donald Trump has pardoned five former NFL players for crimes that include perjury, counterfeiting and drug trafficking. White House pardon adviser Alice Marie Johnson announced the pardons on X Thursday night. She says Trump supports second chances. The White House did not return a request for comment on the reasons for the pardons. The players include Joe Klecko, Nate Newton, Jamal Lewis, Travis Henry and the late Billy Cannon. item.title: All-Star reliever Elroy Face, who saved 3 games for Pirates in 1960 World Series, dies at 97
item.description: Elroy Face, an All-Star reliever for the Pittsburgh Pirates who saved three games in the 1960 World Series to help them upset the New York Yankees, has died. He was 97. In a news release, the Pirates announced they confirmed Face’s death. Team historian Jim Trdinich said the club was contacted by Face’s son, Elroy Jr., and informed the former pitcher died Thursday at an independent senior living facility in North Versailles, Pennsylvania. item.title: Thailand uses a birth control vaccine to curb its elephant population near expanding farms
item.description: Thailand has begun using a birth control vaccine on elephants in the wild to try curb a growing problem where human and animal populations encroach on each other. They say the problem has increased as farms spread into forests and elephants, squeezed in their natural habitat, come into contact and clash with humans while searching for food. item.title: In Zimbabwe, cash bouquets and scrap metal gifts rival flowers as coveted Valentine’s tokens of love
item.description: Zimbabweans are embracing inventive expressions of romance shaped by economic realities as Valentine’s Day approaches. Money bouquets fashioned from U.S. dollar bills are increasingly rivaling fresh flowers. That reflects the premium placed on liquidity in a cash-driven economy. Florists report rising demand across generations while enterprising traders supply crisp replacement notes for decorative use. Recycled scrap metal gifts are also gaining attention. item.title: Palestinians look to salvage Gaza’s history from the ruins of Israel’s military offensive
item.description: The Great Omari Mosque in Gaza City was hit by an Israeli strike during the war with Hamas. It is one of dozens of heritage sites that were damaged or destroyed during the war. With major military operations halted by a shaky ceasefire, Palestinians are gaining a clearer picture of the war's devastation, including the loss of buildings and artifacts testifying to the territory's rich history. item.title: Second US aircraft carrier is being sent to the Middle East, AP source says, as Iran tensions high
item.description: The world’s largest aircraft carrier, the USS Gerald R. Ford, has been ordered to sail from the Caribbean Sea to the Middle East. That's according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke Thursday on condition of anonymity. It comes as U.S. President Donald Trump considers whether to take possible military action against Iran.
